title: helm(private): validate values schema + init hooks for upgrade/rollback
author: Samir Khan
description:
Context and motivation: Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) rely on the helm charts in redwood-helm-charts to provide a smooth install and safe upgrades. Over the last few incidents we observed failures during upgrades where init hooks applied different assumptions about values (missing nested fields, deprecated keys), which caused init jobs to fail and left clusters in partial state. This PR tightens the values schema, improves templating defensiveness, and stabilizes init hooks to be rollback-friendly.

What this PR does (single-line summary): validate values.schema.yaml, add strict defaults and guards in templates, make init hooks idempotent, and add upgrade/rollback compatibility checks and tests.

Highlights (detailed):
- Add values.schema.yaml for `private-installer` helm chart with OpenAPI v3 validation for required nested fields (networking.vpc, storage.backend, installer.upgradePolicy). This prevents misconfigured installs at helm apply time.
- Update templates for init jobs (init-db, init-migrations, init-secrets) to tolerate partial state: check for existing resources, use `helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation`, and set ownerReferences to allow safe rollback.
- Add templating guards around deprecated keys (e.g. `k8s.network` -> `networking`) with explicit warnings emitted as a templated note in Chart NOTES.txt when deprecated keys are present.
- Introduce a small upgrade/rollback test harness in charts/tests that runs `helm upgrade --install` -> fake failure -> `helm rollback` sequences in CI, verifying init job idempotence and resource cleanup.
- Add migration helper in templates/_helpers.tpl to normalize legacy values at render time (non-destructive normalization).
- Improve chart docs (README) with example values and an upgrade checklist.

Checklist:
- [x] values.schema.yaml added and referenced in Chart.yaml
- [x] templates updated with defensive checks and hook delete policies
- [x] tests added to CI that simulate upgrade/rollback failure mode
- [x] CHANGELOG/release notes updated
- [x] Verified locally on a minikube cluster and in a small e2e job on CI

- 0a1b2c3: add values.schema.yaml for private-installer (required networking/storage/installer fields)
- 1b2c3d4: defensive templating for init jobs + hook delete policy

- 3d4e5f6: add helm tests for upgrade/rollback sequences and CI job

Files changed (high-level):
- charts/private-installer/values.schema.yaml (new)
- charts/private-installer/Chart.yaml (chart metadata updated to reference schema)
- charts/private-installer/templates/init-db.yaml (init hook templating hardened)
- charts/private-installer/templates/init-migrations.yaml (init hook templating hardened)
- charts/private-installer/templates/_helpers.tpl (normalization helper)
- charts/private-installer/templates/NOTES.txt (deprecation warnings)

- docs/private-installer/UPGRADE.md (upgrade checklist)

Testing and CI:
- CI added a new job `helm-upgrade-rollback` which runs the tests/upgrade-rollback-test.sh in a privileged test runner.
- Initial CI run failed due to a race in the test harness where the fake failure container did not terminate quickly enough; fixed by adding a readinessProbe and a short TTL in the test job.
- Final CI status: all checks passed (lint, unit, chart-tests, helm-upgrade-rollback).

Review discussion (selected threads):
- Marco Liu: "Can we avoid introducing a full schema that would break older installs that still use the old top-level keys? I'd prefer a schema that validates only when `strictValidation` is true or when `installer.enableSchemaValidation` is set."
  - Samir (author): "Added `installer.strictValidation` flag (default: false). When false, schema will still be present but the chart will run a template-based normalization step that maps legacy keys to new paths so existing installs won't fail. Documented in UPGRADE.md."

- Asha Patel: "init jobs still delete some resources unconditionally in the previous impl; how do we ensure rollback leaves cluster clean?"
  - Samir: "Switched to `hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation` and added ownerReferences for resources created by the hook. Also made all `kubectl` calls idempotent in the tests by checking for resource existence first."

- Elena Garcia: "Small nit: please keep Chart.yaml version bump in a separate commit so release tooling can pick it up."
  - Samir: "Split commit as requested and moved Chart.yaml bump to the final commit before merge."

Edge cases considered:
- Users with older values files: normalization helper tries to map common legacy keys and emits a NOTES.txt warning explaining the mapping.
- Strict installs (CI for enterprise customers): can opt-in to `installer.strictValidation=true` to enforce the schema during `helm install`.
- On-cluster RBAC constraints: init jobs now support `serviceAccount.create=false` mode and will skip creation when not permitted, emitting a clear failure message advising operators.

Release notes:
- Added schema validation for private-installer chart (opt-in via `installer.strictValidation`).
- Init hooks are safer for upgrades and rollbacks; better cleanup and idempotence.
- Deprecation warnings for legacy keys, with automatic normalization.

Merge details:
- PR was approved by Marco Liu and Asha Patel after requested changes were made.
- Final merge method: squash and merge.
- Merge performed by Samir Khan on 2025-02-18.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Expand schema coverage to other charts in the private family (storage, network-provisioner).
- Add a lint rule in CI to warn when adding new top-level deprecated keys.

Full CI summary:
- lint: pass
- chart lint: pass
- unit tests: pass
- helm-upgrade-rollback: pass
- e2e (optional): pass (sanity on minikube)

If anything else is useful for release notes or backporting to the v1.x branch, I can open a follow-up PR that cherry-picks the minimal schema and hook delete policy changes to the v1.x line.
